"If you're worried about the welfare of kids, stop rounding kids up and trying to deport them," said Michael Lukens, executive director of the Amica Center for Immigrant Rights.
In one New York courtroom in April, a judge issued deportation orders for 25 minors in three hours. Some hearings lasted only a few minutes. Among the children was an 8-year-old girl from Ecuador.

The administration has rolled back policies giving immigrant minors access to legal counsel and relief from deportation while they applied to stay. Those policies were built over two decades with bipartisan support to shield children from trafficking and exploitation.

Elder Chavez, 18, holds Special Immigrant Juvenile Status, a protection Congress created for young people abandoned, abused, or neglected by a parent. Alabama police stopped him for speeding, called ICE, and he landed in a Louisiana detention center.
The vast majority of unaccompanied minors removed last year had no criminal history in the United States, according to the analysis of ICE data obtained through public records requests.

Immigration judges are issuing more than 10,000 removal and voluntary departure orders per month for immigrant minors who migrated alone or with relatives. That is nearly four times the rate of Trump's last term.

Immigrant kids who came to the US alone are being detained and removed at about three times the rate of the final years of Trump's first term, a first-of-its-kind ProPublica analysis of ICE data finds. 🧵
